Commentary.Commentary: Back for Ireland's reply. They'll hope to end the day without losing any wickets. Paul Stirling and Cade Carmichael to open for Ireland. Hasan Mahmud to bowl first. Two slips and a gully in place.
...THIRD INNINGS...

For Ireland, it was about maintaining the pressure but as Bangladesh grew into the game, it became harder and harder for the visitors to get a grip. Wickets were hard to come by and they had to work hard for every wicket. Matthew Humphreys scalped five wickets while Barry McCarthy ended with two.

For Bangladesh, the foundation was laid by the openers, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam, who added 168 to the first wicket. Mahmudul Hasan Joy scored his career best 171 while Islam supported him with a wonderful 80. The job wasn't done yet as another massive partnership between Joy and Mominul Haque cut down the deficit without breaking a sweat. This was also the first time Bangladesh's top four batters crossed the 50-run mark in a Test innings.

As the lead crosses the 300 mark, Bangladesh have declared their innings. A solid innings from the hosts. Contributions from mostly every batter has helped them put on a mammoth total against Ireland's 286. From Mahmudul Hasan Joy at the top to Hasan Mahmud down the order, everyone contributed to the total.

Young Humphreys has been the pick of the attack, managing to bag four wickets, but even he hasn't been spared the treatment, leaking quite a few runs in the process. Shanto paired up with Mushfiqur Rahim for a brief stand before the veteran was dismissed for 23. Despite losing those wickets, Bangladesh holds a commanding position, with Litton Das looking assured at the crease. Their current lead stands at a huge 161 runs. With the surface now beginning to offer turn and bounce for the spinners, this total already looks match-winning. All eyes are on the middle now to see how many more vital runs Bangladesh can add to this formidable advantage. Join us at 6.10 am GMT post the Tea Break.

An evenly poised session but Bangladesh are way ahead in the game at the moment. The session certainly brought some joy to the Irish camp, as their bowlers fought back to claim three important wickets. The key breakthrough came early, with Barry McCarthy striking twice in quick succession to dismantle the overnight partnership. First, the brilliant centurion Mahmudul Joy, out for 171, had to depart, followed moments later by his solid partner, Mominul Haque, for 82. However, the action remained positive for the home side, with Najmul Shanto showing great intent and motoring along to a quick half-century.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for the Day 3's play to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mominul Haque will resume their innings. Craig Young will start with the ball. Let's go...

Mahmudul Hasan Joy is in for a chat. He says that the wicket was good for batting, which allowed him to play his natural game. His plan was to settle in during the first few overs, take his time early on, and then start executing his shots once he was set. Joy adds that he has been working on his setup, making adjustments with local coaches. Specifically, he addressed an issue where he tended to shuffle across slightly, and he believes he has improved this aspect of his game. He says that Mushfiqur Rahim is a legend of Bangladesh cricket who shares significant experience with younger players.
Will Bangladesh bat themselves into an insurmountable position, or can Ireland stage a dramatic fightback? Join us as we find out!

The task for Bangladesh this morning is simple, bat Ireland out of the game. Joy and his new partner, Mominul Haque, will be looking to accelerate their scoring, pile on a massive lead, and push towards a declaration. For the Irish bowlers, every wicket will be hard-earned. They need to find a way to break this stubborn partnership early, stem the flow of runs, and give their batters a fighting chance in the second innings.

Yesterday belonged entirely to the home side. After Ireland added a few runs in the morning and were bundled out for a first-innings total of 286, Bangladesh's batters put on a clinic. Their top three were absolutely dominant, but the star of the show was Mahmudul Hasan Joy. His phenomenal, unbeaten innings of 177 has anchored the innings, supported brilliantly by his partners. Bangladesh finished the day at a commanding 338/1, already holding a 52-run lead with nine wickets still in hand.
Welcome back for the third day of the first Test between Bangladesh and Ireland! The sun is shining and we are all set for what promises to be a pivotal "Moving Day" in this contest.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The surface has so far played nicely for the batters, and Bangladesh have certainly made the most of it. The big question is how long it will hold up before it starts to deteriorate, if at all it does. Ireland opted against taking the second new ball late in the day, but you’d expect them to take it straight away in the morning with fresh legs. Their new-ball attack was wayward on Day 2, but the second new ball represents their best chance to make inroads and stay in the game. Thursday, 13th November, will be Day 3 of this Test, with the first ball scheduled for 3.30 am GMT. As always, join us early for all the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Towards the fag end of the day, Mahmudul decided to cut loose, and a chance was created, only for Paul Stirling to put it down when the Bangladeshi opener was on 156. That pretty much summed up the kind of day the Irish had. It was a wicketless third session, with Bangladesh piling on 140 runs in 30 overs at a rate of 4.67. To Ireland’s credit, their discipline improved in the second session after a wayward start in the morning, but as the third session wore on, fatigue began to set in and they struggled to create any real chances, apart from the Stirling drop.

Matthew Humphreys looked the most likely to make something happen, and he eventually did by dismissing Shadman to end the 168-run opening stand. However, that was as good as it got for the tourists, with the pitch offering very little assistance to the bowlers. Shadman missed out on a century, but his opening partner, Mahmudul, carried on to post a career-best 169 and remains unbeaten. Mominul Haque had a few nervous moments early in his innings while attempting the sweep, but he soon settled in and, together with Mahmudul, guided Bangladesh into the lead.

A dream day at the office for Bangladesh! Everything went to plan for the home side from start to finish, while for Ireland it was a long and testing day in the field, one where they had very little to cheer about. Starting the day at 270/8, the visiting side managed to add only 16 runs to their overnight score as Bangladesh swiftly completed the clean-up job. With the ball, Ireland struggled for consistency in their lines and lengths, allowing Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam to make merry at the top of the order.

Post that wicket, it was all Bangladesh again. Mahmudul Hasan Joy is closing in on a well-deserved century, looking very composed, and Mominul Haque has joined him to continue the momentum. Ireland looked deflated towards the end of the session, and they desperately need something special in the third session to swing the game back in their favour. Join us at 8.30 am GMT post the tea break for the final session of Day 2.

SESSION SUMMARY - 31 overs, 89 runs and 1 wicket. What a fantastic session for Bangladesh! They started the session at 109/0 and continued their brilliant dominance. The opening partnership between Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy marched on past the hour mark, continuing to build the foundation. However, Ireland finally found a breakthrough when Matthew Humphreys dismissed Shadman Islam, thanks to a successful review for a faint edge.
A maiden to end the session! Full and at the sticks, Mahmudul Hasan Joy leans ahead and knocks it to mid-wicket. That will be TEA on Day 2!

It is already looking ominous for the visiting side. If they don’t strike early in the afternoon session, it could turn into a long and tiring day in the field for Ireland. They will need to draw inspiration from how Bangladesh clawed their way back in the second and third sessions on Day 1. As for Mahmudul and Shadman, it will be about starting afresh after the break, and having done the hard work to get set, they will now need to make it count. The second session will begin at 6.10 am GMT. See you then!

In reply, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam looked a bit uncertain with their running early on, but soon settled in to provide a solid start. The Irish new-ball pair of Barry McCarthy and Craig Young were all over the place with their lines and lengths, and the Bangladeshi openers made full use of it. It was a similar story with the spinners, who struggled to bowl consistently in the right areas. That allowed the Bangladeshi openers to cruise towards their respective fifties, with Shadman scoring at a quicker rate.

A dominant session for Bangladesh! They wrapped up the Irish innings quickly in the morning and have since made an ideal start with the bat. There is plenty of work to be done ahead for Ireland, who will be disappointed with their discipline with the ball. Jordan Neill and Barry McCarthy showed defiance late on Day 1, but Neill’s dismissal off the final ball of the day left McCarthy and the tail with the task of stretching the total on Day 2. They could add only 16 runs to their overnight score before being bowled out for 286.
